seo.title: Best Viewpoints in Casablanca (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the top 12 viewpoints in Casablanca, Morocco, from panoramic cityscapes to stunning oceanfront terraces. Find the best spots for sunset, iconic landmarks, and unique dining experiences.

hero.subtitle: Casablanca, a city where modern ambition meets coastal charm, offers a diverse array of viewpoints. From towering skyscrapers to historic oceanfront sites, these spots provide breathtaking perspectives of the city, its bustling port, and the expansive Atlantic.

picks.name: Sky 28 (Kenzi Tower Hotel)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Perched on the 28th floor of one of Casablanca's iconic Twin Towers, Sky 28 offers unparalleled 360-degree views of the city. Enjoy signature cocktails and light bites while gazing at the sprawling urban landscape, the Atlantic Ocean, and the majestic Hassan II Mosque in the distance. It's an ideal spot for a romantic evening or a sophisticated start to your night.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic Moroccan mint tea or a specialty cocktail while watching the sunset.
picks.insiderTip: Go just before sunset for breathtaking golden hour views and stay to see the city lights twinkle to life. Reservations are recommended, especially for window seats.
picks.redditQuote: "Sky 28 at the Kenzi Tower is absolutely worth it for the views. Yeah, drinks are pricey, but the panoramic scenery over Casablanca is just unreal, especially at night."

picks.name: Hassan II Mosque Esplanade
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While the interior of the Hassan II Mosque is stunning, the expansive esplanade surrounding it offers magnificent views. Gaze out at the Atlantic Ocean as waves crash against the sea wall, or admire the intricate details of the mosque itself, set against the backdrop of the city. It's a peaceful and inspiring spot for reflection and photography.
picks.whatToOrder: The unobstructed views of the ocean and the mosque's minaret.
picks.insiderTip: Visit early in the morning for fewer crowds and softer light, perfect for photography. Don't forget to walk along the adjacent Corniche for different perspectives of the mosque and coastline.
picks.redditQuote: "The Hassan II Mosque esplanade is honestly one of the most stunning spots in Casablanca. You feel so small next to that masterpiece and the ocean views are incredible."

picks.name: Le Cabestan Oceanfront
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled directly on the oceanfront, Le Cabestan offers an exquisite fine dining experience with dramatic views of the Atlantic. Watch the waves crash against the rocks just meters from your table as you enjoy gourmet seafood and international cuisine. It's a sophisticated venue known for its chic ambiance and unforgettable sunsets.
picks.whatToOrder: Freshly caught seafood and a glass of local Moroccan wine while watching the sunset.
picks.insiderTip: Request a table by the window or on the terrace when making your reservation to maximize the ocean view. It's particularly magical during sunset.
picks.redditQuote: "Le Cabestan is pricey but absolutely worth it for a special occasion. The oceanfront dining experience is unparalleled in Casablanca, felt like I was eating on the water!"

picks.name: Phare d'El Hank (El Hank Lighthouse)
picks.priceRangeLocal: Free (small fee for internal access if available)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Standing proudly at the entrance to Casablanca's port, the El Hank Lighthouse offers fantastic coastal views. While public access to the top is sporadic, the surrounding area provides excellent vantage points of the rugged coastline, the bustling port, and the distant city skyline. It's a great spot for a walk and to capture maritime photography.
picks.whatToOrder: The invigorating sea breeze and the unique perspective of Casablanca's maritime activity.
picks.insiderTip: Walk around the base of the lighthouse and explore the rocky shoreline nearby. It's a popular spot for local fishermen and provides a serene escape from the city hustle.
picks.redditQuote: "The El Hank Lighthouse area is great for a quiet walk. You get amazing views of the ocean and the port entry, very different from the Corniche."

picks.name: Anfaplace Mall Terraces
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Anfaplace is a modern shopping mall located directly on the Corniche. Several of its cafes and restaurants feature spacious terraces that open up to stunning ocean views. Grab a coffee or a quick meal and enjoy the refreshing sea air and the sight of waves breaking on the beach. It's a casual yet scenic spot perfect for a break.
picks.whatToOrder: A traditional Moroccan coffee or fresh orange juice at one of the many cafes with a terrace seat.
picks.insiderTip: Head to the upper levels or the outdoor dining areas for the best unobstructed views. It's less crowded on weekdays.
picks.redditQuote: "Anfaplace's terraces are surprisingly good for ocean views. Grabbing a coffee there and watching the waves is super relaxing after shopping."

picks.name: La Sqala
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Housed within a beautifully restored 18th-century fortress bastion, La Sqala is a renowned restaurant set amidst lush gardens. While not a high-altitude view, it offers charming perspectives of the Old Medina walls, the bustling port, and snippets of the ocean. It's an atmospheric spot to enjoy traditional Moroccan cuisine with a sense of history.
picks.whatToOrder: A full Moroccan breakfast or a tagine for lunch, enjoyed in the garden terrace.
picks.insiderTip: Arrive early for breakfast or lunch to secure a table in the garden, which offers the best views and ambiance. Explore the fortress walls before or after your meal.
picks.redditQuote: "La Sqala's garden setting is absolutely magical, and you get cool views of the port and old city walls. Definitely a must for an authentic Casablanca meal."

picks.name: Le Boudoir (Rooftop Bar)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located in the chic Gauthier district, Le Boudoir is a stylish rooftop bar that offers a lively atmosphere and decent views of the surrounding neighborhood and a glimpse of the city skyline. It's a popular spot for young locals and expats to enjoy cocktails, music, and the vibrant Casablanca nightlife from above.
picks.whatToOrder: One of their creative cocktails or a glass of local beer.
picks.insiderTip: This spot gets busy, especially on weekends, so arrive earlier in the evening to grab a good spot. It's more about the lively ambiance than panoramic views.
picks.redditQuote: "Le Boudoir is a super cool rooftop bar in Gauthier. Not the highest views, but great vibes and you can definitely see the city lights sparkle."

picks.name: Casablanca Marina
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The Casablanca Marina is a modern development offering excellent views of the city's port, luxury yachts, and the impressive Hassan II Mosque from a different angle. Stroll along the promenade, enjoy the modern architecture, and watch the maritime activity. It's a great place for an evening walk and offers several cafes and restaurants with outdoor seating.
picks.whatToOrder: A refreshing walk along the promenade and perhaps a coffee at one of the waterfront cafes.
picks.insiderTip: Visit during the late afternoon to catch the sunset over the marina with the mosque as a backdrop. It's well-lit at night, making it pleasant for an evening stroll.
picks.redditQuote: "The Marina is such a nice addition to Casablanca. Love walking there, seeing the boats and the mosque from that perspective. Very clean and modern."

picks.name: Organic Kitchen (Rooftop)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Known for its healthy and organic menu, Organic Kitchen also boasts a lovely rooftop terrace in the heart of Gauthier. While not a skyscraper view, it offers a pleasant urban vista of the bustling streets and buildings below. It's a relaxed spot for a healthy meal, coffee, or smoothie, away from the street-level noise.
picks.whatToOrder: A fresh smoothie or a healthy brunch item, enjoyed al fresco.
picks.insiderTip: Great for a leisurely brunch or a healthy lunch with a view. The terrace can get quite sunny, so consider a hat or sunglasses.
picks.redditQuote: "Organic Kitchen's rooftop is a hidden gem for a healthy lunch. You get a nice view of the Gauthier area, it's very chill."

picks.name: Basmane Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located directly on the Ain Diab Corniche, Basmane offers traditional Moroccan cuisine in a relaxed setting with direct views of the Atlantic Ocean. It's a popular choice for families and groups looking for good food and a pleasant, accessible oceanfront experience without the formality of fine dining. Enjoy the sea breeze and the sounds of the waves.
picks.whatToOrder: A hearty tagine or couscous dish with a view of the ocean.
picks.insiderTip: Ask for a table on the outdoor terrace for the best ocean views. It's a great spot for a casual lunch after a walk along the Corniche.
picks.redditQuote: "Basmane on the Corniche is a solid choice for Moroccan food with a view. Nothing fancy, but the oceanfront setting is lovely and the food is consistently good."

picks.name: Restaurant Dar Dada
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Tucked away in the labyrinthine streets of the Old Medina, Dar Dada offers a charming rooftop dining experience. While not a panoramic city view, it provides an authentic and unique perspective over the rooftops of the medina, offering glimpses into traditional Casablanca life. Enjoy delicious Moroccan food in an intimate and historic setting.
picks.whatToOrder: The pastilla or a variety of Moroccan salads, best enjoyed on the rooftop terrace.
picks.insiderTip: Finding it can be a bit tricky, so follow Google Maps closely or ask a local. The ambiance and unique view of the medina rooftops are worth the search.
picks.redditQuote: "Dar Dada's rooftop in the Old Medina is such a cool, authentic experience. You really feel immersed looking out over the medina rooftops, and the food is fantastic."

picks.name: Villa Blanca (Rooftop Terrace)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Part of the Villa Blanca hotel, this rooftop terrace offers stunning views of the Atlantic Ocean and the bustling Corniche below. It's a relaxed yet chic spot perfect for a sundowner or a casual meal, combining good service with a fantastic coastal backdrop. Enjoy the fresh sea air and watch the world go by.
picks.whatToOrder: A refreshing non-alcoholic cocktail or a light snack as you enjoy the ocean breeze.
picks.insiderTip: Visit in the late afternoon for a quieter experience and to secure a good table with direct ocean views before it gets busy in the evening.
picks.redditQuote: "The Villa Blanca terrace is a reliable spot on the Corniche for good ocean views. It's chill, not too fancy, perfect for a drink and watching the waves."

faq.question: What's the best time of day to visit viewpoints in Casablanca?
faq.answer: The best time to visit viewpoints in Casablanca is typically during late afternoon or early evening. This allows you to experience the golden hour, witness a beautiful sunset over the Atlantic Ocean, and then see the city lights come alive. Morning visits can also be great for cooler temperatures and fewer crowds, especially at popular spots like the Hassan II Mosque.

faq.question: Are there any free viewpoints in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Yes, several excellent viewpoints in Casablanca are free to access. The esplanade around the Hassan II Mosque offers magnificent ocean and mosque views. Walking along the Casablanca Marina or the Ain Diab Corniche also provides beautiful coastal and city skyline views without any cost. The area around El Hank Lighthouse is also freely accessible.

faq.question: Do I need reservations for rooftop bars or restaurants with views?
faq.answer: For popular rooftop bars and restaurants, especially those known for their views like Sky 28 or Le Cabestan Oceanfront, making a reservation is highly recommended, especially if you want a prime window or terrace seat. Weekends and sunset times are particularly busy, so booking in advance ensures you get the best experience.

faq.question: Are viewpoints in Casablanca accessible for people with mobility issues?
faq.answer: Accessibility varies significantly. Modern venues like Sky 28 and places within Anfaplace Mall are generally wheelchair-friendly with elevators. However, historic sites like La Sqala or the Old Medina (where Dar Dada is located) may have uneven terrain, stairs, or narrow passages. It's best to check with specific venues beforehand or plan for a companion's assistance.

faq.question: Can I get a good view of the Hassan II Mosque from other viewpoints?
faq.answer: Yes, while the mosque's esplanade offers the most immediate view, you can get stunning distant views from other locations. Sky 28 at the Kenzi Tower Hotel provides a fantastic aerial perspective. The Casablanca Marina offers a unique angle looking across the water, and several cafes and restaurants along the Ain Diab Corniche also boast views of the iconic minaret in the distance.

faq.question: What kind of views can I expect in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Casablanca offers a diverse range of views. You can expect panoramic cityscapes from high-rise bars and hotels, expansive oceanfront vistas from Corniche restaurants and coastal landmarks, and charming, authentic views over the traditional rooftops of the Old Medina. The city uniquely blends modern urban scenery with its rich maritime and historical heritage.

methodology: Our selection of Casablanca's best viewpoints was curated through extensive local research, traveler reviews, and expert recommendations. We prioritized locations offering exceptional visual experiences, historical significance, and a range of atmospheres from luxury dining to accessible public spaces, ensuring a diverse and authentic guide for every visitor.
